items.title: Courts reviewing arbitral award on merits defeats purposes of arbitration: Chief Justice Vibhu Bahkru
items.summary: Karnataka High Court Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru on Saturday said that allowing courts to undertake a full merit-based review of arbitral awards would defeat the fundamental purpose of arbitration, which was intended to provide parties with a final adjudication of disputes outside the traditional court system. Speaking at a conference on Ethics and Evidence in Arbitration in Bengaluru, Justice Bakhru acknowledged concerns over the quality of arbitral awards but cautioned against expanding judicial scrutiny. " But if you have a full merits review then automatically the private arbitration is over ," Justice Bakhru said. The conference was jointly hosted by the London Court of International Arbitration (LCIA), ArbitralWomen and the Arbitration and Conciliation Centre Bengaluru at the Karnataka Judicial Academy. Justice Bakhru made the observation during a fireside conversation with Senior Advocate Shashank Garg , a Court Member of the LCIA, on the hits and misses of India's arbitration landscape. items.title: India not yet a preferred arbitration seat, cultural shift needed across judiciary and Bar: Justice Manish Pitale
items.summary: Bombay High Court judge Justice Manish Pitale stated that India is currently not featuring as a preferred seat for international commercial arbitration and judiciary, legislature, and the legal profession must work in tandem to drive institutional change. The judge delivered the special address at the ICC India Arbitration Conference in Mumbai. ICC india Arbitration Conference 2026 Justice Pitale noted that international disputants evaluate whether a jurisdiction's domestic legal framework aligns with global standards before selecting an arbitral seat. “India, at the present moment, is obviously not featuring there as one of the preferred seats. What's the reason for this? Where are we going? It's something we need to think about,” he said. items.title: Kerala High Court Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas completes Ironman 70.3 triathlon in Goa
items.summary: In what is likely a first for the Indian judiciary, sitting High Court judge, Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas , completed the gruelling Ironman 70.3 triathlon which was held in Goa this past weekend. An Ironman 70.3, also known as a Half Ironman, is organised by the World Triathlon Corporation. The 70.3"refers to the total distance in miles (113.0 km) covered in the race, consisting of a 1.2-mile (1.9 km) swim, a 56-mile (90 km) bike ride, and a 13.1-mile (21.1 km) run. Kerala High Court judge Justice Bechu Kurian Thomas competed in the men's 55-59 years category and completed the race with a time of 8:46:44. items.title: Indian scientist secures patent for in-vivo power generator after Bombay High Court order against IIT
items.summary: The Indian Patent Office has formally approved a patent for scientist Dr. Tarkeshwar Chandrakant Patil, securing his exclusive ownership over an invention capable of generating electrical power inside the human body. This outcome follows a September 8 order of the Bombay High Court in Patil’s decade-long dispute with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay. The dispute involved an apparatus and a method for in-vivo power generation, a technology designed to keep medical implants active inside the human body. Patil’s patented device functions by converting glucose found in cerebrospinal fluid into a hydrogen-rich fuel, such as ethanol or methanol, using bioenzymes. This fuel powers a nano-scale biofuel cell implanted in the body, creating a self-sustaining power source that mitigates the need for repeated surgeries to replace traditional lithium-ion button batteries. IIT Bombay initially filed the patent application in August 2013. However, after internal disputes, the institute executed a worldwide assignment deed in 2017 transferring all intellectual property rights to Patil.
